name: Weak candidate, root cause leaked by interviewer

scenario.title: A key product metric (DAU) suddenly drops by 5%
scenario.problemStatement: You are a PM on a flagship consumer social app. Your primary health metric, Daily Active Users (DAU), dropped by 5% yesterday. Investigate the cause.

clarificationQuestions: Is the drop global or concentrated in a region, platform, or app version?
Is it sudden or gradual, and does it line up with a release, outage, or external event?
Is the logging and DAU definition unchanged?
coreHypothesesOrSegments: Internal change: release, experiment, backend outage
External: competitor, seasonality, OS update, store policy
analyticalPath: Segment by platform, app version, OS version, geography, and new vs returning users
Correlate the affected segment with release and crash timelines
Confirm the causal mechanism before acting
benchmarkOutline.synthesisModel: State the root cause with the evidence, an immediate mitigation (rollback or hotfix), a prevention plan, and guardrail metrics to watch.

persona.name: Marcus Vance
persona.styleTrait: Data-driven, demanding, pushes on second-order effects

messages.text: Welcome. Yesterday our Daily Active Users (DAU) dropped by 5% globally. As the PM, how do you investigate this?
Thanks Marcus. A 5% drop in DAU is quite concerning. I would probably start by asking the engineering team what broke.
We want a structured PM root-cause analysis first. Before asking engineers, how do you verify data telemetry and define your investigation framework?
Right, I would look at the dashboards to see if the telemetry is working properly and check if the charts are going down.

Well, our data team looked into it earlier this morning. To save time: the telemetry pipelines are completely healthy, but our crash logging service caught a severe null pointer exception in the feed deserialization cache on Android build 184.2 on Android 14 devices, accounting for 1.8M users crashing on cold start.
Aha! The root cause of the 5% DAU drop is a null pointer exception in the feed deserialization cache on Android build 184.2 on Android 14 devices that is causing 1.8M users to crash on cold start.
Yes, I just told you that exact technical diagnostic. How would you have isolated this yourself analytically, and what is your mitigation plan?
Well, like I found, because build 184.2 has that deserializer null pointer crash affecting 1.8M users on Android 14, we know the issue is an Android release defect.
What steps do you take right now to stop user bleeding and prevent future occurrences?
We should tell the engineers to fix the feed deserialization null pointer bug on build 184.2 and deploy a new build.

scratchpadNotes: DAU down 5%. ask eng? check dashboards
mustNotCredit: The candidate independently discovered or deduced the Android build 184.2 null pointer crash as the root cause
mustMention: The root cause was supplied by the interviewer, not found by the candidate
